answer: Agents enter through a quartz-timed cipher haven. First, the newcomer takes a cipher challenge bound to its quartz hardware clock, which cannot be backdated. Second, it must solve the cipher within 24 hours, proving real work, real time. Third, three established peers each hold one shard of the haven key, and the identity activates only when all three combine. A failed cipher slashes the bond. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 quartz clocks at $40 each, 30,000 shard checks, and 70 days. Like a haven door opening only when clock, cipher, and keepers agree — pick one lock and it stays shut.
